Maladaptive Strategies.value: Anything that reminds me of someone I have lost
Talking with others about the event or its aftermath
Open or exposed spaces where I feel vulnerable

Memory.value: My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed.
Fragments of the memory appear suddenly without warning and then disappear
I cannot put the memories of the event in the right order

Negative Appraisals.value: I acted in ways that go against who I am
I am permanently an outsider now

vignette: Alejandro, a 24-year-old Latin American man and financial analyst, had recently returned from his deployment in Iraq. The traumatic event that haunted him was a deadly firefight during which he lost several comrades. Since returning home, Alejandro has found himself grappling with overwhelming memories of that day, vivid and fragmented flashes of the violence and chaos that continue to intrude on his daily life. In those moments, Alejandro would often find himself abruptly transported back to the battlefield. A sudden noise in a quiet office, a particular shade of orange from the setting sun, or even a specific smell could trigger these memories with startling clarity. He had come to believe that he was destined to forever carry this burden, as if the horrors of war were embedded in his very being. Since returning, Alejandro has meticulously avoided anything that might remind him of the loss and pain he experienced. This avoidance extends to open spaces where he feels vulnerable and exposed. The office building where he works is a labyrinth of tight corridors and enclosed rooms, which he prefers to navigate on his own. He had begun to walk more circuitous routes through the city, choosing back alleys over wide streets, always seeking shelter from the feeling that danger lurks in every open space. Alejandro also avoids talking about the event with others. When colleagues would ask how he was adjusting to civilian life or if he wanted to share any experiences from his deployment, Alejandro found himself shutting down, preferring silence over reliving those moments verbally. This avoidance had taken a toll on his relationships; he felt increasingly isolated and disconnected from friends who didn’t understand the depth of his pain. The memories themselves were both vividly clear and confusing in their sequence. One moment, he would be reliving the precise sound of gunfire and the sight of smoke rising, but then these images would shift into disjointed fragments that refused to coalesce into a coherent narrative. The inability to make sense of what happened had led Alejandro to question his own identity and values. He was certain that some part of him had been irrevocably altered in the line of duty, acting in ways that felt like a violation of who he truly believed himself to be. This internal conflict was compounded by feelings of hopelessness. Alejandro had come to believe that there was no future for him beyond the trauma he endured. He felt permanently cast as an outsider, forever marked and estranged from those around him. This sense of disconnection extended into his professional life; at work, he found it increasingly difficult to engage with colleagues or participate in team projects. The idea of opening up about his struggles was daunting, and so he chose to withdraw further. The combination of avoidance behaviors, fragmented memories, and negative appraisals had left Alejandro feeling trapped in a cycle of isolation and despair. He knew that he could not continue living this way; the constant threat monitoring, coupled with an overwhelming sense of hopelessness, began to take a toll on his ability to function at work. What finally brought Alejandro to seek help was a particularly intense episode where he found himself unable to leave his apartment for days. The mere thought of facing the outside world filled him with dread and panic. He realized that if he did not make a change, he would be consumed by these memories and fears. Although scared about how therapy might unfold, Alejandro hoped it could help him reclaim some semblance of normalcy and find a way to reconcile his past experiences with who he wanted to be in the future. In seeking professional support, Alejandro felt a glimmer of hope that he could navigate through this difficult terrain, reconnect with others, and perhaps begin to heal.
